    AI Overview
    "For" is
    a versatile preposition and conjunction primarily used to indicate purpose, reason, destination, duration, or support. It connects actions to their goals ("run for health"), indicates recipients ("a gift for you"), or shows duration ("waited for hours"). It also means "because" or "in exchange for". 
    Key Uses of "For": 
    • Purpose/Intention: Indicates the reason for an action or an object's function (e.g., "tools for building," "ran for exercise").
    • Duration/Distance: Expresses how long or far (e.g., "lived there for five years," "walked for miles").
    • Recipient/Beneficiary: Identifies who receives something (e.g., "This letter is for you").
    • Support/Agreement: Indicates being in favor of someone or something (e.g., "She voted for the proposal").
    • Exchange/Price: Represents a trade (e.g., "bought it for
      ").
    • Because/Reason (Conjunction): Used to introduce a reason (e.g., "I went to bed, for I was tired"). 
    Common Confusions: 
    • For vs. To: Use "for" before a noun (e.g., "for lunch") and "to" before a verb (e.g., "to eat").
    • For vs. Since: Use "for" for a duration of time (e.g., "for 3 days") and "since" for a specific starting point (e.g., "since Monday").
